findings.message: The client-supplied file name is interpolated into a shell command run with shell=True, so a name like `x; rm -rf ~` executes arbitrary commands. It also allows path traversal (`../`) outside UPLOAD_DIR, both for reading the source and writing the target.
findings.suggestion: subprocess.run(["convert", str(UPLOAD_DIR / client_name), "-resize", "128x128", str(UPLOAD_DIR / target)], check=True)

findings.message: client_name is not validated, so values containing path separators or `..` escape UPLOAD_DIR. Reject names that are not a plain basename, or names whose resolved path is not inside UPLOAD_DIR. Names starting with `-` can also be read by ImageMagick as options, and prefixes like `msl:` can be read as coders.
This new behaviour has no accompanying test, but the contributing guide requires one for every change in behaviour.
